Dynamic penetration (DPT) test on RS soil; apparatus: DPT 1.59 lb 2-3/4 inch body dropped 25.4 inch; loading: dynamic penetration (free drop). Recorded: deceleration vs time.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 102 of the 109 points, and the rest were settled against the scan. They have not yet been checked by a person. The report labels the soil state differently in two places (RS-Dense). The test setup is incomplete: relative density Dr, fill depth, rate are not reported.
:::

## Data

![deceleration against time, SI units. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-dpt-r54-65.png){.lightbox}

Peak deceleration 763.1 m/s^2 at 14.8 ms time; 12.81 m/s^2 at 88 ms, the end of the record.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-dpt-r54-65/observations.csv) (109 points: 0 plotted symbols, 102 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1 (Fig. 2-54): deceleration in m/s^2 against time in s; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-dpt-r54-65/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on this figure (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 0.356 ms in time, 4.79 m/s^2 in deceleration (Fig. 2-54) (0.6 percent of the peak). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 102 of the 109 points; the other 7 were settled against the scan (read by one reader and verified by the other, or decided between two readings). [Check the digitized points against the scan](../figures/index.qmd#check-f2-54).

**About these values.** The figure prints no time origin: time is counted from the timing line that carries the three deceleration rulers (0 ms), so only differences of time are measured; the timing lines are 10 ms apart (the figure's 0.01 s bar). Deceleration is in g as printed (G's), positive upward, converted with standard gravity; 0 g is each ruler's printed zero, not the dashed line drawn about 0.7 to 1.0 g above it. Samples are in drawing order and may share a time on a steep flank.
